newsitem.title: INDIA: India bond seen fully-bid, yield at 10.75-10.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: India bond seen fully-bid, yield at 10.75-10.9 pct.

text.p: A forthcoming Indian government bond auction is likely to be fully subscribed and dealers said they expected the cut-off yield to be between 10.75 and 10.90 percent.

"I think the yield will be around 10.75 percent," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The central bank has taken the market by surprise once...those expecting higher yields may burn their fingers once again."
Earlier this month, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) set a cut-off yield of 11.83 percent for a six-year bond against market expectations of 11.90-11.95 percent.
"I expect yield on the new paper to be slightly higher, around 10.90 percent, if it is to go through in full," said the treasury head of a state-run bank.
He said the larger size of the auction will force the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to accept a slightly higher yield than those prevailing in the secondary market.
The government on Tuesday announced a 50 billion rupee auction of four-year bonds for July 28.
Auctions held earlier this year have been for amounts ranging from 20 billion rupees to 30 billion rupees.
"As the amount is bigger, the RBI will have to be a bit more flexible," the treasury head said. "Otherwise it may end up having to pick up some of the paper itself."
Dealers said the tenure of the bonds will also play an important part in determining the nature of bids and pricing.
"Typically, the insurance companies and provident funds look for paper with longer maturities," said a dealer at a private sector bank.
"A good deal of the bids (for the four-year bonds) will be from foreign banks and private banks," he said. "And they will be looking for higher yields."
Dealers said the current easy liquidity with the banking system will ensure success of the auction.
Banks have been stuck with a problem of rapid deposit growth and poor demand for credit through 1996/97 (April-March) and in the current financial year so far.
The latest Reserve Bank of India (RBI) figures show total bank deposits at 5,214.42 billion rupees on July 4, 1997, an increase of 775.89 billion over the year-ago figure.
Bank advances however grew by only 243.68 billion rupees in the same period to 2,774.60 billion.
